questions.q: In Mo Gawdat’s happiness formula, what is subtracted from the events of your life?
a: Your expectation of how life should be
The opinions of the people around you
The amount of money you earn
Your memories of past successes
questions.why: The overview states the formula as happiness being the events of life minus your expectations of how life should be.

questions.q: What does the summary say the voice inside your head actually is?
a: An internal version of the speech you use with other people
A direct message from your true self
A separate personality living in your mind
A sign that you are mentally unwell
questions.why: Lesson 1 draws on Vygotsky to argue inner speech is external speech turned inward, not the real you.

questions.q: What is the real you, once you strip away possessions, friends, body and identity?
a: The invisible observer of the world
The sum of your strongest memories
The voice that criticizes you most
The role you play at work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says only the invisible observer remains, and no one can take that away.

questions.q: Why does the brain use filters, according to the summary?
a: Taking in all sensory information would be too much to handle
Filters make sure you notice every detail around you
Filters are a modern flaw with no useful purpose
Filters keep you focused only on threats
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that filters select sensory input because processing everything at once would overwhelm the brain.

questions.q: What did Matt Killingsworth’s happiness study find?
a: The more people focus on the present moment, the happier they are
People who plan for the future are the most content
Happiness depends mainly on income and status
Mind-wandering makes people calmer and less anxious
questions.why: Lesson 3 reports that present-moment focus predicted happiness regardless of whether life was going well.
